The errors are out of 94 English words, 162 Japanese characters, 33 Arabic, 41 Portuguese, 31 Russian and 28 Turkish words per set; N below is that count. Two pass rules:

- First rule, written before any of these numbers, on set A alone: per language, at most the reference's errors plus max(2, ⌈0.03 × N⌉), and the speaker, UTMOS22 and end-of-speech checks of the next rule, taken against reference set A. The Mac CPU run failed it on English (6 errors against a bar of 4) and passed its other checks; the phone's set A errors are within its bars.
- Rule applied here, written after that result and before any set B run of these graphs: per language, the errors of sets A and B together at most the reference's A and B errors plus max(2, ⌈0.03 × 2N⌉) (bars: en 10, ja 10, ar 12, pt 9, ru 3, tr 4); on set B, each speaker group's mean cosine at least the reference's minus 0.05, the UTMOS22 mean at least the reference's minus 0.10, at most 21 of the 30 sentences more than 0.02 below the reference's UTMOS22 on the same sentence, and every sentence ended by end of speech. The Mac CPU run passes it (Arabic errors 12 against a bar of 12), and so does the phone (Arabic errors 8 against a bar of 12).

The Mac run used ai-edge-litert 2.2.0 (Interpreter, 4 threads) on an Apple M4 Max, the slow graph at a KV cache of 2,048 positions and the Preview's codec decoders. With a KV cache of 1,024 positions, the slow graph gives bit-identical logits and hidden states on the 38 prompts tested (the 30 above and 8 more), and the rewritten decoders give byte-identical CPU output. The phone run is the app with the files of this repository's first release, the codec on the GPU and the slow AR's KV cache in the app's ping-pong mode (two buffer sets, each call reading one and writing the other); updating that cache in place gives the same codes on both phones (the two speed-test sentences, every run).

The slow file of this release is the same export with a `prefill_64` signature added. On the Mac CPU its `prefill_256` and `decode` give bit-identical outputs to the first file's on the 38 prompts; a prompt prefilled as 256 positions plus one `prefill_64` call leaves the same KV cache and logits as 256 positions plus a padded `prefill_256` call (12 of 12 runs), a prompt of up to 64 positions gives the same outputs through `prefill_64` as through a padded `prefill_256` (4 of 4), and the host loop makes the same codes with either file (4 of 4 sentences). In the app, the current file read from its weight cache made the same codes as the first file without a cache (12 of 12 runs on each phone).

Not shipped, measured on the same test: int4 weights in the slow AR. Four int4 recipes made an AR frame (one slow `decode`, ten fast steps) 4.6 to 15.2 % faster in our runner on the two phones, and none passes the rule above on the Mac CPU. The first (int4 in blocks of 32 on every linear layer) fails it on Turkish (8 errors against a bar of 4), Arabic (14 against 12) and UTMOS22 (3.834 against 3.864). The other three, each tested as a file with this repository's int8 prefill and its own int4 decode, fail it on set B's UTMOS22 (3.750, 3.801 and 3.850 against 3.864). The Preview repository's int8 codec decoder lowers UTMOS22 from 3.904 to 3.690 on the same codes, on every one of the 30 sentences.

## Limitations

- The prompt (reference transcript, reference codes and text) plus the generated frames must fit the slow graph's KV cache of 1,024 positions. The host loop refuses a longer prompt and stops when the cache is full; the app refuses a sentence over 49 tokens, and its longest prompt (49 tokens and a 10 s voice recorded in the app) is 320 positions with the English recording script and 324 with the Japanese one, which leaves room for the 512-frame cap.
- At most 512 frames (23.8 s of speech) per call by default; the host loop stops there and prints a `[cap]` line, and the app says so in its message (an 80-token English text reached the cap in 2 of 2 runs on the Mac and lost its last sentence).
- The codec decoder is causal, but its transformer works on 128-frame windows, so decoding in windows is not sample-exact against one offline decode of the whole utterance. The host loop and the app make one 128-frame call up to 5.9 s of speech, one 192-frame call up to 8.9 s, and beyond that 192-frame windows with 128 frames of left context.
- Voice registration takes up to 10 s of reference audio (the encoder has one fixed length), and the transcript must match the audio.
- Record the reference voice in the language it will speak. With the bundled English voice, 9 of the 10 other languages tested had a sentence with two or more word errors (Arabic, Finnish, Hindi, Indonesian, Norwegian, Swedish, Thai in characters, Turkish, Vietnamese; Malay had none), 21 of the 30 sentences in all, and the source model's own code had 17 of 30 on the same sentences and voice. With a Swedish reference voice, 15 of 15 Swedish runs (5 sentences, 3 seeds) had no word errors. Measured on the Mac with the host loop and this repository's first files (2026-11-02).
- The accuracy test covers 6 of the 23 languages (English, Japanese, Arabic, Portuguese, Russian, Turkish). The other 17 were not tested on these files.
- Speed was measured on one Galaxy S26 and one Pixel 11 Pro with our runner and app; other devices were not measured. The Mac numbers are agreement checks, not speed.
- From the source model card: quality varies by language; noisy reference audio or a mismatched transcript can reduce stability and speaker similarity; speech may contain pronunciation errors, repetitions, omissions or early stopping, so listen to it before using it. Obtain permission to clone a voice, and disclose synthetic audio where appropriate.

Source: [`Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air`](https://huggingface.co/Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-Air) (the old name `Edge0/Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b` redirects to it) at revision `1e857568bfd4f02931aca3988ee773a44d2d26d3`; the three later commits on its main branch (`925bbd4c` on 2026-11-01, `7c82ad18` and `23c305cc` on 2026-11-02) change only `README.md` and `assets/realistic-hero.svg`. **Changes from the original work.** The slow and fast AR transformers were exported from the checkpoint's weights to LiteRT graphs with the KV cache as graph inputs and outputs, and their weights quantized to dynamic int8.
